title: Greyhound Normal Values
desc: Breed-specific reference intervals from Idexx — chemistry, haematology and total T4 — alongside the general canine ranges. No weight or medication needed.

notes.How to read this: Each entry is GREYHOUND-SPECIFIC first, then the general canine interval in brackets. Source: Idexx greyhound reference intervals. A greyhound result that looks abnormal against the general canine range is frequently normal for the breed.
notes.The big four to remember: Greyhounds normally run a HIGHER haematocrit, HIGHER creatinine and SDMA, and LOWER platelets, white cells and T4 than other dogs. Reading those against general canine ranges is what leads to unnecessary work-ups.
notes.Chemistry — renal: SDMA 0–20 µg/dL (general 0–14) · Creatinine 1.2–2.1 mg/dL (0.5–1.5) · BUN 13–29 mg/dL (9–31)
notes.Chemistry — electrolytes: Chloride 107–117 mmol/L (108–119) · Potassium 3.8–4.7 mmol/L (4.0–5.4) · Sodium 139–149 mmol/L (142–152) · Na/K ratio 31–39 (28–37) · TCO2 (bicarb) 18–25 mmol/L (13–27) · Anion gap 12–20 mmol/L (11–26)
notes.Chemistry — minerals & glucose: Glucose 72–118 mg/dL (63–114) · Calcium 9.3–10.5 mg/dL (8.4–11.8) · Phosphorus 2.3–5.1 mg/dL (2.5–6.1)
notes.Chemistry — protein: Total protein 5.2–6.8 g/dL (5.5–7.5) · Albumin 2.7–3.9 g/dL (2.7–3.9) · Globulin 2.2–3.5 g/dL (2.4–4.0) · Alb/Glob ratio 0.9–1.5 (0.7–1.5)
notes.Chemistry — bilirubin: Total bilirubin 0.2–0.5 mg/dL (0–0.3) · Conjugated 0–0.1 mg/dL (0–0.1) · Unconjugated 0.1–0.4 mg/dL (0–0.2)
notes.Endocrinology: Total T4 0.5–1.7 µg/dL (general canine 1.0–4.0). A greyhound with a T4 in the low-normal general range is usually euthyroid — do not diagnose hypothyroidism on total T4 alone in this breed.
